examples.japanese: {右|みぎ}の{耳|みみ}に{水|みず}が{入|はい}った。
examples.english: Water got in my right ear.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}は{耳|みみ}がいいので、{小|ちい}さい{音|おと}も{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: Dogs have good hearing, so they can detect even quiet sounds.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}くなったので、{電話|でんわ}ではいつも{大|おお}きく{話|はな}さないと{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: My grandmother has become hard of hearing, so on the phone I always have to speak loudly or she can't understand.

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}に{乗|の}った{時|とき}、{耳|みみ}が{痛|いた}くなったので、{水|みず}を{飲|の}んだら{少|すこ}しよくなった。
examples.english: When I got on the plane, my ears started hurting, so I drank some water and felt a little better.

notes:
{耳|みみ} refers to the ear, the organ of hearing.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {耳|みみ}が{痛|いた}い: ear hurts
- {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い: hard of hearing
- {耳|みみ}にする: to hear about
- {耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}ける: to listen attentively
- {耳|みみ}をすます: to listen carefully

IDIOMS:
- {耳|みみ}が{早|はや}い: quick to hear news
- {耳|みみ}にたこができる: to hear something repeatedly (lit. "to get a callus on one's ear")
- {馬|うま}の{耳|みみ}に{念仏|ねんぶつ}: preaching to deaf ears

RELATED BODY PARTS:
- {目|め}: eye
- {鼻|はな}: nose
- {口|くち}: mouth
